title: 'The Cathedral and the Bazaar' and the Case for Open Collaboration (1997)
explainer: Eric Raymond's 1997 essay, drawn from his experience maintaining the fetchmail project and observing Linux kernel development, argued that open, loosely coordinated ('bazaar') development could outperform tightly controlled ('cathedral') development for certain kinds of software. The essay is widely credited with helping persuade Netscape to open-source its browser code in 1998, making it one of the clearest historical arguments for why the large-scale collaboration this lesson teaches actually works in practice.
